description: Expected results for the official pyGIMLi example '2D ERT modelling and inversion' (doc/examples/3_ert/plot_01_ert_2d_mod_inv.py, gimli-org/gimli git tag v1.5.5.post1, commit d0ed6ed4, the same release as the installed engine). The script builds a 2-layer + 2-anomaly resistivity model, simulates 171 dipole-dipole readings on 21 electrodes with fixed noise (1% + 1 uV, seed=1337), inverts them on an automatic unstructured mesh (lam=20) and on a custom regular grid (lam=20). inputs/ holds the unmodified official script. The first inversion is also re-run through the KI tool tools/run_pygimli.py on the script's own simple.dat and read with tools/parse_gimli_output.py.
engine_version: pygimli 1.5.5.post1 + pgcore 1.5.5 (pip wheels in the dissection venv), Python 3.12

official_checks.name: ki_chi2
official_checks.why: upstream assert in the script: np.testing.assert_approx_equal(mgr.inv.chi2(), 0.7, significant=1) for the first inversion (lam=20); significant=1 here means |chi2-0.7| < 0.1

official_checks.name: inv_grid_chi2
official_checks.why: upstream assert in the script: assert_approx_equal(mgr.inv.chi2(), 1.4, significant=2) for the regular-grid inversion; means |chi2-1.4| < 0.1

reference: official_checks are the upstream values asserted inside the official script (with the upstream tolerance, |chi2-value| < 0.1). numeric_checks were recorded from our own real runs (12 clean runs of the script, 4 runs of the KI tool). Exactly repeatable every time: simulated data (simple.dat byte-identical), mesh, the regular-grid inversion, and the KI-tool inversion of simple.dat. NOT bit-repeatable: the script's own first inversion (automatic mesh) gave 3 slightly different results (chi2 0.70378/0.70379/0.70821, min 22.9602-22.9664, max 146.710-146.741), so those two checks have wider tolerances; all stay inside the upstream assert.
notes: No change to the official script. Only the matplotlib backend is set to Agg (env var) so no windows open; this does not touch any numbers. The KI tool reads simple.dat as saved by the script; the file stores values with limited digits, so its model min/max differ from the script's own by about 1e-5 Ohm m.
